name: Mahāyāna
regions: historically Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia

tradition.text: Taught by the Buddha Śākyamuni himself; some sūtras were withheld (e.g. kept by the nāgas) and brought forth later when there were beings able to receive them

scholarly.text: Mahāyāna sūtras appear from c. 1st c. BCE / 1st c. CE (first Chinese translations by Lokakṣema, c. 179 CE; Gāndhārī Prajñāpāramitā fragment c. 1st-2nd c. CE); composition continued to c. 5th c.

transmissions_received.what: the Buddha's teaching, the Vinaya ordination lineages (Dharmaguptaka in East Asia, Mūlasarvāstivāda in Tibet) in which Mahāyāna monks and nuns were ordained

transmissions_given.what: the Prajñāpāramitā sūtras as scriptural basis of emptiness
the Saṃdhinirmocana and Laṅkāvatāra as basis of the ālaya and three-nature doctrines
the Laṅkāvatāra, Vajracchedikā and Vimalakīrti as early Chan scriptures
the Lotus as the final and complete teaching
the Avataṃsaka as the Buddha's first, unconcealed teaching
the bodhisattva path, bodhicitta and emptiness as the ground of the Mantrayāna ('the perfection vehicle' as its cause)

distinctive_positions: The goal is the full awakening of a buddha (anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi) for the sake of all beings, not the personal nirvāṇa of the arhat; the practitioner is a bodhisattva who vows to liberate all beings
All dharmas are empty (śūnya) of own-being (svabhāva), unborn and like an illusion — including the aggregates, the path and nirvāṇa itself (Prajñāpāramitā)
The six (or ten) perfections, grounded in the perfection of wisdom and in skillful means, are the path
The three vehicles are the Buddha's skillful means; there is ultimately one buddha-vehicle (Lotus, Śrīmālā) — or, per other sūtras, beings have fixed lineages (gotra) (Laṅkāvatāra, Saṃdhinirmocana)

The Buddha is not only the historical teacher: his dharmakāya is suchness; his lifespan is immeasurable and his parinirvāṇa a skillful display (Lotus 16, Mahāparinirvāṇa); countless buddhas teach in buddha-fields in the ten directions
All beings possess the tathāgatagarbha / buddha-nature (Tathāgatagarbha sūtras, Mahāparinirvāṇa)
The sūtras themselves are objects of worship: where a sūtra is kept or taught is a shrine (caitya); copying, reciting and teaching them is supreme merit
Saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, defilement and purity, are not two (Vimalakīrti); the bodhisattva does not abandon saṃsāra (non-abiding nirvāṇa)
summary: The 'Great Vehicle': the body of sūtras and the movement, within the Buddhist monastic and lay communities of India from around the turn of the common era, that takes the bodhisattva's path to full buddhahood for all beings as the highest aim, teaches the emptiness of all dharmas, skillful means, innumerable buddhas and buddha-fields, and (in some sūtras) the buddha-nature in all beings. It became the Buddhism of East Asia and Tibet. This umbrella entry covers the sūtra layer; the scholastic schools (Madhyamaka, Yogācāra), Pure Land, Chan/Zen, the Chinese schools and Vajrayāna have their own entries.
notes: parent set to lin:early-buddhism for lineage-root purposes (the Mahāyāna did not arise as a separate ordination lineage: its monastics were ordained in the Nikāya Vinayas). The tradition itself regards the Mahāyāna sūtras as the word of the Buddha; the scholarly account treats them as later compositions.

name: Tathāgatagarbha (Buddha-nature) tradition
alt_names: de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po / bde gshegs snying po (Tibetan)

tradition.text: Taught by the Buddha in the 'third turning' (Tibetan) / in his last teaching before parinirvāṇa (Mahāparinirvāṇa); the Ratnagotravibhāga taught by Maitreya to Asaṅga (Tibetan account)

scholarly.text: Tathāgatagarbha sūtras c. 3rd c. CE (Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra, Śrīmālā, Mahāparinirvāṇa core); Ratnagotravibhāga c. 4th-5th c.; Chinese translation 511

transmissions_received.what: the Mahāyāna path and the Prajñāpāramitā teaching of emptiness, which the Tathāgatagarbha texts re-read ('empty of adventitious stains, not empty of the buddha-qualities')
the luminous mind (pabhassara citta) obscured by adventitious defilements (AN 1.51-52)

transmissions_given.what: buddha-nature, the one mind, 'seeing the nature'
the tathāgatagarbha as the one mind (Awakening of Faith)
buddha-nature of all beings, including insentient (Zhanran)
shentong: the dharmakāya empty of other
buddha-nature as ground of Mahāmudrā (Gampopa, Rangjung Dorje)
buddha-nature as the ground (gzhi) in Dzogchen
buddha-nature read as the emptiness of the mind (a naturally abiding lineage), the RGV read through Madhyamaka

distinctive_positions: All sentient beings have (or are) the tathāgatagarbha: the embryo/womb of the Tathāgata, the buddha-element (dhātu) or buddha-nature, covered by adventitious defilements (Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra; RGV 1.27-28)
The dharmakāya is permanent, blissful, self and pure — the four perfections of qualities (Śrīmālā; Mahāparinirvāṇa; RGV 1.35)
The garbha is empty of the separable defilements and not empty of the inseparable buddha-qualities (Śrīmālā ch. 9; RGV 1.154-155)
The realm of beings neither increases nor decreases; the sattvadhātu, the tathāgatagarbha and the dharmakāya are one (Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa)
Buddha-nature was taught to remove five faults: discouragement, contempt for others, grasping the unreal, denying the real, and excessive self-love (RGV 1.156-157)
The one vehicle is final (Śrīmālā); even icchantikas have buddha-nature (later Mahāparinirvāṇa)
summary: The strand of Mahāyāna sūtras and treatises teaching that every sentient being contains the tathāgatagarbha — the buddha-nature, the pure dharmakāya obscured by adventitious defilements — which, once cleansed, is revealed as a buddha endowed with permanent, blissful, self-like and pure qualities. In India it was never a separate school; its sūtras and the Ratnagotravibhāga were read into Yogācāra and Madhyamaka, and it became central to East Asian Buddhism (Awakening of Faith, Chan, Huayan, Tiantai) and to Tibetan debates on buddha-nature (rangtong/shentong).
notes: Status 'absorbed': not an independent institutional lineage; the teaching lives on in the Chinese, Korean, Japanese and Tibetan schools listed in transmissions_given.
